anchor: Which he beside the rivulet
note: Rivulet: a small stream or brook.

anchor: Who stood expectant by
note: Expectant: waiting eagerly to see or hear something.

anchor: Who fell in the great victory
note: The skull is a relic of Blenheim, where many thousands died in 1704.

anchor: The ploughshare turns them out
note: Ploughshare: the blade of a plow that cuts the soil.

anchor: With wonder-waiting eyes
note: Eyes wide with curiosity, waiting to hear the old man’s answer.

anchor: And what they fought each other for
note: Blenheim was part of the War of the Spanish Succession, fought to decide who would inherit the Spanish throne. Kaspar’s ignorance is part of the joke.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Marlborough, John Churchill, 1st Duke of”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Marlborough%2C_John_Churchill%2C_1st_Duke_of

anchor: Who put the French to rout
note: Rout: a crushing defeat in which an army flees in disorder.

anchor: But what they fought each other for
note: Kaspar repeats that he never understood the war’s cause, though he lived through its damage.

anchor: every body said
note: Quoth: said (an old word).

anchor: My father lived at Blenheim then
note: Blenheim was a village in Bavaria where, in 1704, an English army under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugène of Savoy defeated the French.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Blenheim”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Blenheim; Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Marlborough, John Churchill, 1st Duke of”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Marlborough%2C_John_Churchill%2C_1st_Duke_of

anchor: They burnt his dwelling to the ground
note: Dwelling: a house or home.

anchor: With fire and sword the country round
note: A stock phrase for war that burns and kills across whole regions.

anchor: Was wasted far and wide
note: Wasted: laid waste, destroyed. War ruined whole districts, not only armies.

anchor: And many a childing mother then
note: Childing: about to bear a child.

anchor: Lay rotting in the sun
note: After the battle the dead lay unburied across the field.

anchor: Great praise the Duke of Marlbro’ won
note: The Duke of Marlborough was the English commander at Blenheim. Parliament built him a great mansion, Blenheim Palace, as a reward.

anchor: And our good Prince Eugene
note: Prince Eugène of Savoy commanded troops at Blenheim and fought beside Marlborough against the French and Bavarians.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Marlborough, John Churchill, 1st Duke of”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Marlborough%2C_John_Churchill%2C_1st_Duke_of

anchor: “Why ’twas a very wicked thing!”
note: Wilhelmine’s blunt moral judgment puts the child’s view against the old man’s.

anchor: But what good came of it at last?
note: Peterkin’s question gives the poem its point: he sees no good in it.

anchor: My days among the Dead are past
note: The Dead: here, the great writers of the past, whom the scholar knows through their books.

anchor: Where’er these casual eyes are cast
note: Casual: here, idle and unplanned.

anchor: My never-failing friends are they
note: The scholar’s friends are the books of the dead, and they never fail him.

anchor: With whom I converse day by day
note: Converse: to talk, here through reading.

anchor: With them I take delight in weal
note: Weal: well-being, good fortune, prosperity.

anchor: My cheeks have often been bedew’d
note: Bedew’d: moistened as if with dew, here wet with tears.

anchor: Their virtues love, their faults condemn
note: Condemn: to declare wrong or blameworthy.

anchor: Partake their hopes and fears
note: Partake: to share in, to take part in.

anchor: Instruction with an humble mind
note: Instruction: teaching or lessons. The scholar learns humbly from the dead.

anchor: My hopes are with the Dead; anon
note: Anon: soon, in a short while.

anchor: And I with them shall travel on
note: He expects to join the dead and travel on with them through time.

anchor: Through all Futurity
note: Futurity: the time to come, the future.

anchor: That will not perish in the dust
note: Perish: to die, to be destroyed. He hopes his name will outlast his body.
